Patient demographics:
  age: 44
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Asian
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Chef
  trauma_type: Refugee
  pcl5: 42

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Emergency Contexts: Ambulances, Crash Discussions: Talk about accidents, Visual (Injuries): Visible injuries or wounds on others
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Uniform or Weapons: Military, police uniforms or weapons, Avoid Open Spaces: Open or exposed spaces where I feel vulnerable, Fawn Response: become overly compliant when feeling threatened
  Threat: Concentration: Having difficulty concentrating, Hypervigilance: Being superalert or watchful or on guard, Escape Route Planning: I always identify escape routes before I feel comfortable anywhere
  Memory: Nonverbal Memory: I can't seem to put the frightening event into words., Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger, Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
  Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened, Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not, Permanent Damage: I have permanently changed for the worse

Vignette:
Rohan had always taken pride in his work as a chef, whipping up intricate curries and delicate naan breads with ease. But these days, even the simplest tasks felt like a struggle. It had been two years since he fled his home country, seeking refuge from the violence that had ravaged his community. Rohan's memories of that time were fragmented, but one moment stood out in vivid detail: the sound of gunfire and screams as his family's small grocery store was overrun by armed men. Since then, certain sights and sounds had become potent triggers for Rohan. The wail of an ambulance siren could send him into a panic, transporting him back to that chaotic day. He couldn't bear to watch news reports about accidents or violence, and would quickly change the channel if someone started discussing a recent tragedy. Even seeing visible injuries on others - a cut hand, a bruised cheek - made his stomach turn. As a result, Rohan had developed a range of strategies to avoid these triggers. He stopped wearing his crisp white chef's coat, fearing it might remind him of military uniforms. He avoided walking through open spaces, opting instead for narrow alleys and side streets that made him feel safer. When he did venture into crowded areas, he found himself constantly scanning the surroundings, searching for potential escape routes. Despite these efforts, Rohan couldn't shake the feeling of being "on guard" all the time. He had trouble concentrating on even simple tasks, his mind constantly racing with worst-case scenarios. His friends and colleagues began to notice a change in him - he was more withdrawn, more easily startled. When someone asked for help or offered support, Rohan would become overly compliant, eager to please but also secretly feeling trapped. Rohan's memories of the traumatic event itself were hazy, but when they did surface, they left him numb and disoriented. He might recall the sound of gunfire, only to feel like he was observing it from afar, disconnected from his own emotions. Other times, the grief would overwhelm him - he would think about all that he had lost, all the people who didn't make it out alive. Rohan couldn't forgive himself for not doing more to protect his family and community. He felt guilty for surviving when so many others did not. He began to wonder if he was permanently damaged, if the trauma had altered him in some fundamental way. These thoughts swirled through his mind like a toxic stew, leaving him feeling exhausted and defeated. It wasn't until Rohan's restaurant started to struggle - customers complaining about slow service, staff members frustrated with his increasingly erratic behavior - that he realized he needed help. He couldn't keep living like this, constantly looking over his shoulder, waiting for the next shoe to drop. As he sat in his dimly lit apartment, surrounded by the familiar smells of spices and oil, Rohan felt a glimmer of hope. Maybe, just maybe, he could learn to confront these demons head-on, to find some measure of peace amidst the chaos.
